travel.label: Travel
main: My favourite weekends begin with a train ticket and no firm plan for where I end up.
I keep a battered notebook of small discoveries from every trip, like a bakery that opens at dawn or a bridge with a good view.
I would rather get lost in a new neighbourhood for an afternoon than tick off a list of famous sights.
Learning ten useful phrases before a trip is my idea of homework I actually enjoy.
Night markets, slow ferries and cheap guesthouses are my kind of luxury.
I plan the first day of a trip and leave everything after that to curiosity.
Airports at six in the morning feel like the start of something to me.
I collect small maps from places I have visited and they are slowly taking over a wall.
Taking the long way home, even on an ordinary day, is a habit I never grew out of.
I am happiest when I can point at a map and say that is where we should go next.
minor: I save up for one big trip every year.
Travel stories make the best conversation.
I always say yes to a spontaneous day trip.
A half packed suitcase is a good sign for me.

cooking.label: Cooking
main: Sunday afternoons usually find me with a pot of something slow on the stove and music on.
I bake bread at weekends and I am still arguing with my sourdough starter.
Cooking for friends is how I say thank you better than I can with words.
I read recipes the way other people read novels, with a pen in hand.
My spice shelf is out of control and I regret nothing.
I will happily spend an hour on a sauce and ten minutes eating it.
The farmers market is my weekly ritual, and I always come home with more than I planned.
I am trying to master a proper omelette before I turn my attention to anything fancier.
A shared kitchen, a loud playlist and a pile of onions to chop sounds like a perfect evening.
I make soup whenever the weather turns, and I am generous with the portions.
minor: I cook most nights and rarely follow a recipe exactly.
Leftovers for lunch are one of life's quiet joys.
I like trying a new ingredient every week.
My kitchen is small but it gets a lot of use.

music.label: Music
main: There is almost always a record playing in my flat, and I am happy to explain why it is good.
I play guitar badly but with great enthusiasm, mostly for an audience of houseplants.
Live shows in small rooms where you can see the drummer sweat are my favourite kind of night.
I make playlists for every mood, journey and bad day, and I take requests.
Finding a song nobody else has heard yet gives me a ridiculous amount of joy.
I sing in the shower, in traffic and, if pressed, at a party.
My taste runs from jazz trios to loud electronic sets, and I do not see a contradiction.
I still buy albums and read the liner notes, which my friends find charming or alarming.
Learning piano as an adult is humbling and I recommend it.
I could talk for an hour about why one particular bass line is perfect.
minor: Music is on from the moment I wake up.
I go to more concerts than is sensible.
Ask me for a song recommendation and see what happens.
I hum while I cook and I am told it is tuneful.

fitness.label: Fitness
main: I run early, before the city wakes up, and it is the highlight of my day.
Climbing at the indoor wall twice a week keeps me stubborn and strong.
Last year I entered a half marathon and found that I like the training more than the race.
Swimming laps clears my head better than anything else I have tried.
I stretch more than I should admit, usually while watching something silly.
My idea of a date includes a long walk, a hill and a reward at the top.
I am slowly getting better at yoga, which means I fall over less often.
Cycling to work is the only commute I have ever liked.
Strength training taught me that patience works better than motivation.
I track my runs, but only because I enjoy beating last month's slowest pace.
minor: I work out most mornings.
Active weekends suit me best.
A friendly volleyball game is an easy yes from me.
A tired body and a quiet mind is my favourite combination.

outdoors.label: Outdoors
main: Give me a trail, a thermos and a reasonable sunrise and I am set for the day.
I camp whenever the forecast allows and sometimes when it does not.
I know the names of more trees than people, which is a fair summary of my character.
Kayaking on flat water in the evening is as close to a perfect hour as I know.
I keep a small pack by the door so a hike is never more than a decision away.
Stargazing from a cold field is worth every layer of clothing it requires.
I like the kind of walk where nobody talks for twenty minutes and nobody minds.
I am learning to read the weather from the clouds and I am right about half the time.
A campfire, a tin mug of tea and a decent story is my kind of night.
Fresh air fixes more problems than most things I have tried.
minor: Whenever the weather allows, you will find me out of doors.
Rain is not a good enough reason to cancel a hike.
I have strong opinions about good hiking socks.
Sunrise from a hilltop beats any alarm clock.

books.label: Books
main: My to read pile has its own shelf, and it keeps winning.
I love a long novel that you can disappear into for a rainy week.
I annotate in the margins and I have no apology for it.
A good second hand bookshop can swallow my whole afternoon.
I read on the train, in the bath and, shamefully, while walking.
I run a tiny book swap with a few friends and the arguments are half the fun.
Short stories are my secret favourite because they leave room for you to think.
I will lend you a book, but I will remember who has it.
Reading aloud to someone you like is underrated.
I keep a list of sentences I wish I had written.
minor: Most of my reading is fiction, and there is plenty of it.
Ask me what I am reading and settle in.
My favourite place is a corner with a lamp and a book.
I buy more books than I finish, and I accept it.

technology.label: Technology
main: I build small tools for myself at weekends, most of which only I will ever use.
I get unreasonably excited about a well designed interface.
Taking apart an old gadget to see how it works is my idea of fun.
I tinker with a home server, a few sensors and a plant that now reports its water level to my phone.
Debugging feels a bit like detective work, and I find it deeply satisfying.
I follow open source projects the way some people follow sports teams.
My favourite problems are the ones that look simple and turn out to be hiding something.
I automate small annoyances, then spend longer on the automation than the annoyance ever took.
I like explaining technical ideas in plain words, and I get better at it each time.
Learning a new programming language every year keeps me humble.
minor: I work with computers and I like it.
I am the person friends text when their wifi breaks.
I enjoy a good puzzle, digital or otherwise.
Gadgets with too many buttons make me happy.

family.label: Family
main: Family dinners on Sundays are loud, long and one of my favourite things in the world.
I talk to at least one relative most days, and I am very close to all of them.
Building a home with plenty of noise, mess and shared jokes is the goal.
I babysit my nieces and nephews, and apparently I am the fun relative.
Holiday traditions matter to me, even the slightly ridiculous ones.
The idea of a life with kids in it someday, and a dog, and a messy garden, appeals to me.
Being reliable for the people I love is the thing I am proudest of.
I call my grandparents every week and I always learn something.
A house that smells of cooking and has someone asleep on the sofa sounds right to me.
Home, for me, is wherever the people I love are sitting around one table.
minor: My family sits at the centre of how I spend my time.
Time with the people closest to me comes first.
I love a crowded table.
Weekends often involve a relative or two.

humour.label: Humour
main: I laugh at my own jokes half a second before the punchline, which ruins them and delights me.
I collect terrible puns and deploy them without mercy.
A friend once called my sense of humour dry; I think it is simply well aged.
I would rather share a ridiculous story than a polished one.
Quick banter, slow burn teasing and the occasional silly voice are all part of the package.
The best conversations are the ones where we both end up laughing too hard to finish a sentence.
I do a very convincing impression of a confused seagull.
Life is too short to take every email seriously.
I keep a mental list of funny things people say, and I quote them fondly.
Self deprecating humour is my native language, and I am working on being kinder to myself.
minor: I laugh easily and often.
Please bring a sense of humour and a spare pun.
Taking myself seriously has never been my strong suit.
Good banter is a deal breaker, in the best way.

creative.label: Creative work
main: I sketch on the back of receipts, and my bag is full of them.
I am halfway through a novel I have been writing for three years, and that is fine.
Painting badly in a messy corner of my flat is the best therapy I have found.
I take photographs of ordinary doorways and I could explain why for a long time.
Making things by hand, from ceramics to wonky bookshelves, is how I relax.
Writing short poems on the bus is a habit I picked up and cannot drop.
I go to galleries on weekdays, when it is quiet enough to hear yourself think.
I am learning to print on fabric and my kitchen is covered in ink.
There is a half finished project on every flat surface of my home.
I believe everyone has a creative streak, and I like helping people find theirs.
minor: I make something most weeks.
Creative work pays my bills and I love it.
My notebook goes everywhere with me.
There is always some project in progress around me.

volunteering.label: Volunteering
main: I help out at a community garden on Saturday mornings and the tomatoes are getting ambitious.
I volunteer at a local shelter and it has changed how I spend my free time.
I mentor a young person once a week and I get more from it than they do.
Neighbourhood clean ups are weirdly satisfying, and the group is lovely.
I believe in showing up, even when it is inconvenient.
I teach basic computer skills at the library, and the questions are wonderful.
I donate blood regularly and I always take a snack.
Being useful to other people is one of the surest routes to feeling good that I have found.
I organise a small monthly food drive and I am always recruiting.
I care about the place I live, and I try to act like it.
minor: I volunteer a few hours each month.
I like giving back where I can.
Community matters a lot to me.
The people around me can count on me to show up.

pets.label: Pets
main: My dog decides the schedule in our home, and I have made my peace with it.
I have a cat who judges my life choices from the top of the bookshelf.
Long walks with a four legged companion are the best start to any day.
I foster rescue animals when I can, and I have learned to say goodbye with a smile.
I stop to meet every dog on the street, and I apologise in advance.
My home is covered in fur and I consider it decoration.
Ideally I meet someone who accepts that my animals come as a package.
I talk to animals as if they are colleagues.
I can tell you the name, breed and personality of every dog in my building.
A sleepy animal on my lap makes me feel I am doing life correctly.
minor: A pet who is firmly in charge shares my home.
Animals are my favourite people.
I am a dog person who is open to cats.
Pet hair on my clothes is a permanent accessory.

openers: Hello there, I am glad you found this page.
I am a curious person who likes small adventures.
This is my attempt at describing myself without sounding like a brochure.
Quick sketch: friendly, slightly reserved for the first ten minutes, chatty after that.
Strangers tend to chat with me on trains, so I assume I am approachable.
Here is a short, honest summary of me.
I keep revising myself, and I enjoy the editing.
My friends call me warm, stubborn and an excellent listener.
I believe in kindness, good conversation and second helpings.
Most days I am calm and occasionally chaotic.
I tend to overthink and then laugh about it.
I am more at ease in small groups than at big parties.
closers: If some of this sounds familiar, come and say hello.
Tell me about something you are excited about right now.
A good conversation is what I am hoping for.
Send a note if you would like to swap stories.
Tell me what has been keeping you curious lately.
Bring your favourite recommendation and we can go from there.
That is the short version, and I am happy to tell you the long one.
Write back if something here made you smile.
Meeting people who are open to new things is a pleasure.
Let us see where a conversation goes.
